newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner to sell stake in American Lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner to sell stake in American Lawyer.

text.p: Time Warner Inc said Wednesday it will sell its interest in American Lawyer Media, a publisher of legal magazines and newspapers, and Counsel Connect, an online service for lawyers, as part of its previously announced strategic plan to sell non-core assets to reduce debt.

The company also said American Lawyer Media founder and chief executive Steven Brill sold his share of the American Lawyer Media and Court TV partnerships back to Time Warner following the company's decision to keep its interest in Court TV, a "valuable asset" of its cable networks group.
The company said it chose not to sell its interest in Court TV and American Lawyer Media together to a group that would have been led by Brill.

For that reason, he will leave American Lawyer Media in approximately six months, after assisting Time Warner with the sale of the American Lawyer Media publications and online service and assuring an orderly transition at Court TV.
Brill currently heads Court TV, which is owned by Time Warner, General Electric Co unit NBC and Liberty Media Corp LBTYA.O.
Thayer Bigelow, president and CEO of Time Warner Cable Programming, will ultimately assume the role of chief executive of Court TV, reporting to Time Warner vice-chairman Ted Turner.
